entries.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository as the calf-raise family base: standing with the balls of the feet on the step and the heels free; the ankle travels from the owned stretch to a full rise while the whole leg chain stays rigid (every bone exactly constant), and a dumbbell rides each hand. The cue line mentions one dumbbell plus a balancing hand; both bells are drawn per the implement line (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a standing dumbbell calf raise on a step, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Stand with the balls of the feet on the step, heels free.
Lower into an owned calf stretch and pause.
Rise tall over the big toe.
Reach the top of the rise with the ankles.
Hold the top for a beat.
Lower slowly along the same path.
Sink back into the stretch.
Neutral again; ready for the next rep.

entries.name: Calf Raises - With Bands
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the hands were held about waist height. Source-bound side-view draft: standing on a band with a handle in each hand beside the shoulders; the forefeet stay planted and the heels rise as far as the ankles allow, so the whole body lifts with straight legs, a pause, and a slower lowering. The hands do not move against the shoulders, and the band only stretches as the body rises. Not drawn: the hip-width stance, which a side view cannot show.
entries.summary: Standing on a band with the handles beside the shoulders, root the forefeet and rise as high as the ankles allow with the hands quiet, pause, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Stand on the middle of a long band with the handles held at shoulder height and the feet set about hip width.
Root the forefeet and rise as high as the ankles allow while the hands stay quiet beside the shoulders.
Pause. Own the top.
Lower slowly into an owned stretch.
If the hands bob to manufacture height, the calves have stopped driving the rep.

entries.name: Calf Raise On A Dumbbell
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from the public-domain free-exercise-db entry and its two photographs, with a deliberate safety change to a stationary non-rolling dumbbell, awaiting the owner; the catalogue's own text is a placeholder on a source hold. Drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: flat hexagonal dumbbell heads that cannot roll, the ball of the working foot on the handle, the other foot clear of the floor, both hands on the fixed bar in front, and the working heel moving from below the handle to full extension while the dumbbell stays still.
entries.summary: Using a dumbbell that cannot roll (hexagonal heads, or wedged) checked for stability on the floor and holding a support that cannot move with both hands, stand with the ball of one foot on the handle and the other foot lifted, keep the dumbbell still and the knee straight as you lower the heel into a stretch, rise into full calf extension and hold for a second, then lower under control.

frames.caption: Use a dumbbell that cannot roll (hexagonal heads, or wedged) on the floor in front of a sturdy support that cannot move, check it is stable before stepping on, hold the support with both hands, and stand with the ball of one foot on the handle and the other foot lifted clear of the floor.
While the dumbbell stays still and the knee stays straight, lift the heel to rise on the ball of the foot over the handle into a full calf extension.
Contract the calf hard at the top and hold for a second while the dumbbell stays still.
Lower the heel under control back into the stretch while the dumbbell stays still, complete the repetitions, then change legs.
Use a dumbbell that cannot roll, check it is stable before stepping on, and hold a support that cannot move.

entries.name: Standing Barbell Calf Raise
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 18 degrees: lowering into a deep stretch with a full bottom pause, driving up over the big toe as high as balance allows with a top pause, and returning under control.
entries.summary: With a barbell across the upper back and the balls of the feet on a stable low block with the heels free, lower into a deep stretch and pause at the bottom, then drive up over the big toe as high as balance allows and pause at the top.

frames.caption: Set the bar across the upper back with a tall body and place the balls of the feet on a stable low block with the heels free.
Lower the heels below the block into a deep, owned stretch.
Hold a full pause at the bottom stretch with the bar quiet on the back.
Drive up over the big toe to rise as high as balance allows.
Hold the top pause at full height with a tall body.
Lower under control back to the starting position on the block.
